title: SAS tokens, shared keys and the container that leaked

videos.script: Every request in the last four lessons was signed with one key. That key can read, write and delete everything in the account. {{key}} This lesson is about handing out less than that. {{less}} A shared access signature is a permission written into a URL. One blob, read only, for thirty minutes. You will use one with no key at all. {{sas}} Then you will try to stretch it: another file, a write, a later time. Each one is refused. {{refused}} A signature like that cannot be taken back before it expires. A stored access policy can, and you will revoke one in a single command. {{revoke}} Then the setting that makes a container readable by anybody on the internet. It is one command, and so is undoing it. {{public}} And the container that leaked. It is almost never a break-in. It is a setting, a link that lived too long, or a key left in a file. {{leak}} By the end you can harden an account so that none of the three is possible. {{end}}
